No AI-attributable headcount number anywhere in the filing; hedged risk-factor language filed ~3 months after a cut the March termination emails explained only as 'a broader organizational change'. 141k is a NET year-end figure (gross cuts offset by OCI/AI hiring). Press coverage framed the cuts as funding the ~$50B FY26 AI capex push (Nvidia GB300, AMD MI355X, 4.5GW Stargate buildout tied to OpenAI's $300B compute contract), but the widely-circulated Catz ('generational reallocation of capital') and Ellison ('choosing the chips') quotes could not be traced to any real source and are likely fabricated. The cuts happened despite Q3 FY26 GAAP net income of $3.7B (+27% YoY) and RPO of $553B (+325% YoY). M&A CONTEXT (verified vs 10-Ks, 2026-07-13): Oracle's workforce grew only via acquisition, not organic hiring — headcount went 143k (FY22, pre-close) to ~164k (FY23) after buying Cerner (June 2022, ~25-26k employees); organic headcount actually shrank ~4-5k. Oracle has cut Cerner/Oracle Health repeatedly since (documented rounds 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 per Becker's/Healthcare IT News); the Kansas City campus fell from 12,778 employees (Feb 2022) to ~6,400 (May 2024) BEFORE this round. The only company-confirmed Oracle Health figure for 2026 is a 539-person Kansas City WARN filing (eff. May 26/Jun 1). The viral '8,000-10,000 Cerner specialists' / '30% of Revenue & Health Sciences' figures are UNRELIABLE — traced to anonymous Reddit/Blind posts amplified by a recruiting-agency blog, same provenance rot as the fabricated exec quotes above; not used.
